original_question: Fix nonnegative integers a1, a2, …, an. For a graph G of order n, let ci denote the number of cycles of length i in G, and let f(a1, a2, …, an) be the maximum possible number of edges in a graph satisfying ci ≤ ai for every i. Determine f(a1, a2, …, an) for the general cycle-length distribution constraint problem.
target_in_paper: Section 1 ("Erdös Problem"), the unnumbered open problem on page 3 immediately after Conjecture 1.16 and before Theorem 1.17: Shi's problem of determining f(a1, a2, ..., an) from the cycle length distribution (c1, c2, ..., cn) of a graph of order n.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's main target very closely: it fixes nonnegative integers a1, a2, ..., an; it uses ci for the number of cycles of length i in a graph of order n; it defines f(a1, a2, ..., an) as the maximum number of edges under the constraints ci ≤ ai; and it asks to determine that extremal function. This is exactly the open problem attributed to Shi in Section 1.
missing_details: The paper ties the parameter list (a1, a2, ..., an) to a graph G of order n, so the quantifier should explicitly begin with a fixed positive integer n and fixed nonnegative integers a1, a2, ..., an.
The cycle length distribution should be stated as the full sequence (c1, c2, ..., cn), where ci counts cycles of length exactly i for every 1 ≤ i ≤ n.
To make the question fully stand-alone, it is helpful to say 'graph on n vertices' rather than relying only on 'order n'.
The paper presents this problem as an extension of Erdős' original problem, and explicitly notes the special case f(n) = f(1, 1, ..., 1).

The nearby context also records that determining ex(n, Ck) is a special case of determining f(a1, a2, ..., an); this is part of the paper-faithful scope-setting, even though it is not an alternate statement of the whole problem.
There is no asymptotic clause such as 'for sufficiently large n' in the statement of Shi's problem itself.
No ambient ring, field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency data are relevant here, because the target statement is a finite extremal graph problem rather than an algebraic one.
refined_question: Fix a positive integer n and nonnegative integers a1, a2, ..., an. For a graph G on n vertices, let (c1, c2, ..., cn) be its cycle length distribution, where ci denotes the number of cycles of length i in G. Determine f(a1, a2, ..., an), the maximum possible number of edges in a graph G satisfying ci ≤ ai for every 1 ≤ i ≤ n.
justification: The draft is aimed at the unnumbered problem statement in Section 1, page 3. There the paper defines the cycle length distribution (c1, c2, ..., cn) of a graph G of order n, defines f(a1, a2, ..., an) as the maximum number of edges in a graph satisfying ci ≤ ai, and says that Shi posed the problem of determining f(a1, a2, ..., an). The same paragraph explicitly says that this extends Erdős' original no-repeated-cycle-length problem via f(n) = f(1, 1, ..., 1), and the following lines note that ex(n, Ck) is a special case of determining f(a1, a2, ..., an). Theorem 1.17, immediately afterward, supplies a nearby worked special case f(0, 0, 2, ..., 2). So the paper-faithful refinement is not a broader 'general constraint problem' but exactly the finite extremal problem of determining the function f(a1, a2, ..., an) defined from the cycle length distribution.
